front_blocks.md: What are the six steps of the descriptive writing structure?

back_blocks.md: **Panoramic** (whole scene) → **zoom** (one detail) → **single line** (key feeling) → **shift** (another part) → **shift** (a final part) → **panoramic** (scene changed)

front_blocks.md: How should you use your time in the descriptive writing task?

back_blocks.md: Spend **10–15 minutes planning** (mind-map or table), then leave **five minutes** at the end to re-read and correct mistakes.

back_blocks.md: A **five-part story structure**: exposition (set the scene) → rising action (build tension) → climax (turning point) → falling action (consequences) → resolution (ending)

front_blocks.md: How do you keep your story plot manageable in the exam?

back_blocks.md: Plan **one main event** and **one main setting**, with no more than **two characters**; avoid long timescales and multiple plot twists.
